basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Binds an authority to a delimited competence along territorial, personal, material and temporal axes, not just to a territory.
Differs from an administrative unit or place, which describe space; a jurisdiction describes the power to make, judge or enforce rules.
Differs from applicable-law determination: it records competence, not which law governs a particular dispute.
Records the conferring instrument and evidence for every delimitation, so overlapping claims can be traced.

may: Register a jurisdiction record with its conferring instrument and evidence.
Align the record to ISO 3166, UN M49 or another external territorial code.
Resolve candidate jurisdictions for a place, person or subject matter and report overlaps.
Record succession, cession or dissolution as a new state with dates.
mustNot: Decide which authority actually prevails in a conflict of competence.
Treat a territorial code as proof of legal competence.
Infer jurisdiction from a person's IP address, language or location alone.
Overwrite historical scope when borders or competences change.
Present a disputed or unrecognised claim of authority as settled.
requiresHuman: Resolving overlapping or contested claims of competence.
Recording recognition of a disputed territory or authority.
Registering an immunity or exception that removes a person or matter from a jurisdiction.

considerations: Jurisdiction determines which courts, police and tax authorities can act on a person; errors can deny access to justice or expose people to the wrong authority.
Disputed territories carry political weight; a record must show the dispute rather than take a side silently.
Indigenous and minority legal orders may be overlooked if only state authorities are modelled.
affectedParties: People and organizations subject to the authority
Communities in disputed or transferred territories

items: A jurisdiction record names an authority-holder, a type of power, a scope on four axes and the instrument that confers it.
Often confused with a country, an administrative region, a court and the governing law of a contract.
Filing, reporting or enforcement directed to an authority without competence.
Stale records after succession or boundary change misroute legal obligations.
Silent resolution of disputed claims misleads agents and users.
ISO 3166-1 and ISO 3166-2 country and subdivision codes.
UN M49 standard country or area codes.
European Legislation Identifier (ELI) and European Case Law Identifier (ECLI).
